rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sībawayh says the echo suffix follows the final vowel: wāw after ḍamma, yāʾ after kasra, alif after fatḥa; a final consonant cluster is broken by moving the consonant.
rows.anchor: فالزيادة تتبع الحرف الذي هو قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The suffix marks a challenging echo that can reject the speaker’s position, express surprise, or deny that a reported event occurred.
rows.anchor: فتقول أزيدنيه غير راد عليه متعجبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attach the suffix once at the end of the entire echoed utterance, including a coordinated phrase or an adjective.
rows.anchor: قلت أزيدا وعمرنيه تجعل العلامة في منتهى الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A following vocative such as يا فتى is outside the reported utterance and prevents the suffix from attaching, as other endings are dropped in that connection.
rows.anchor: وإن قلت أزيدا يا فتى تركت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some Arabs insert إن between the name and suffix to make the marker clearer, since the hāʾ and yāʾ are otherwise faint.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن من العرب من يجعل

rows.speaker: رجل من أهل البادية
rows.claim: Sībawayh reports a Bedouin answering أنا إنيه when asked whether he would go out once the steppe became lush, illustrating denial of the questioner's assumption.
rows.anchor: وسمعنا رجلا من أهل البادية قيل له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker may echo the actual words or append the marker to wording that conveys the intended correction; the marker may also be omitted.
rows.anchor: الزيادة ما لفظ به وتحكيه مبادرة له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not use the echo suffix when asking for confirmation or guidance rather than rejecting the reported statement.
rows.anchor: إذا قال ضربت زيدا فإنك لا تلحق الزيادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With fatḥa, أن has four uses: it can nominalize a clause, mean أي, be redundant, or be a lightened form of heavy أن.
rows.anchor: فإن مفتوحة تكون على وجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إن can mark a conditional clause or introduce a statement in an oath context, as in the cited Qur'anic examples.
rows.anchor: فتكون للمجازاة وتكون أن يبتدأ ما بعدها في معنى اليمين

rows.speaker: رجل من أهل المدينة موثوق به
rows.claim: A trusted Medinan informant reports hearing an Arab say إن زيد لذاهب; Sībawayh identifies this lightened إن with the form in the cited verse.
rows.anchor: عن رجل من أهل المدينة موثوق به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In إن الكافرون إلا في غرور, إن means ما, giving the sense “the disbelievers are only in delusion.”
rows.anchor: أي ما الكافرون ~~إلا في غرور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction ما إن زيد ذاهب has an independent initial clause; Sībawayh cites Furwa ibn Maysik's ما إن طبنا as poetic evidence.
rows.anchor: وقال فروة بن مسيك # % وما إن طبنا جبن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For one three-letter pattern, a mass or collective noun takes a feminine -ة form for an individual, as in صخر/صخرة.
rows.anchor: فأما ما كان على ثلاثة أحرف وكان فعلا فهو نحو طلح والواحدة طلحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Use the singular with -ات for a small number; for many, use the collective noun itself.
rows.anchor: فإذا أردت أدنى العدد جمعت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some such unit nouns also take a broken plural on فعال, as with سخلة/سخال, بهمة/بهام, and طلحة/طلاح.
rows.anchor: وربما جاءت الفعلة من هذا الباب على فعال وذلك قولك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some speakers pluralize صخرة as صخور, by analogy with بدرة/بدور and مأنة/مؤون.
rows.anchor: وصخور فجعلت بمنزلة بدرة وبدور ومأنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same unit-and-collective pattern applies to nouns with weak wāw or yāʾ, which show forms such as مرو/مروة, صعوة/صعو/صعاء, and شرية/شري.
rows.anchor: فمثل مرو ومروة وسرو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some doubled nouns form unit/collective pairs such as حبة/حب and قتة/قت; a second three-letter pattern likewise forms pairs such as بقرة/بقر and شجرة/شجر.
rows.anchor: ما كان على ثلاثة أحرف وكان فعلا فإن قصته كقصة فعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Weak nouns also show variants such as حصى/حصاة/حصيات, قطاة/قطا, and أضاة/أضا/إضاء; Sībawayh says إكام-like forms were analogized to رحاب.
rows.anchor: ونظير هذا من بنات الياء والواو حصى وحصاة وحصيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forms such as حلق/حلقة and فلك/فلكة are rare; adding the feminine marker lightens the unit form and changes its meaning.
rows.anchor: وقد قالوا حلق وفلك ثم قالوا حلقة وفلكة

rows.speaker: يونس عن أبي عمرو
rows.claim: Yunus reports Abu Amr's usage of حلقة as an alternative form.
rows.anchor: وهذا قليل وزعم يونس عن أبي عمر و أنهم يقولون حلقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A less frequent pattern has no attested broken plural beyond the collective form; examples include نبقة/نبق and خربة/خرب.
rows.anchor: إلا أنا لم نسمعهم كسروا الواحد على بناء سوى الواحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Several other patterns form unit nouns and collectives, usually with regular -ات plurals; Sībawayh gives examples including عنبة/عنب, سمرة/سمر, and بسرة/بسر.
rows.anchor: وأما ما كان فعلا فهو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word نعر names a disease affecting camels in their heads.
rows.anchor: والنعر داء يأخذ الإبل في رءوسها

rows.speaker: أبو الخطاب
rows.claim: Abu al-Khattab says the singular of طلى is طلاة, with -ات used for a small number; Sībawayh also gives حكأة and مرعة as unit forms.
rows.anchor: وزعم أبو الخطاب أن واحد الطلى طلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some speakers form a broken plural سدر from سدرة, analogizing it to forms such as لقحة/لقاح and طلحة/طلاح.
rows.anchor: وقد قالوا سدرة وسدر فكسروها على فعل

rows.speaker: المسيب بن علس
rows.claim: Sībawayh cites al-Musayyib ibn Alas's الحقق as poetic attestation for the plural of حقة.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر وهو ~~المسيب بن علس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same unit-and-collective pattern covers دخنة/دخن and doubled forms such as درة/در, with درر also attested as a broken plural.
rows.anchor: ومثل ذلك من المضاعف در ودرة ودرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Where أن can occur, أنما can also occur; the clause after أنما is its complement, like the clause after the relative الذي, and أنما does not govern it.
rows.anchor: اعلم أن كل موضع تقع فيه أن تقع فيه أنما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'anic phrase يوحى إلي أنما إلهكم إله واحد illustrates أنما after a clause where أن إلهكم إله واحد would also work.
rows.anchor: إلي أنما إلهكم إله واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn al-Itnaba's verse uses أنما in a dependent construction where an أن clause could replace it.
rows.anchor: وقال الشاعر ابن الإطنابة # % أبلغ الحارث

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil says إنما is not a noun; it is non-governing and must introduce an independent clause.
rows.anchor: فأما إنما فلا تكون اسما وإنما هي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thus وجدتك إنما أنت صاحب كل خنى is valid as an independent clause after وجدتك, while وجدتك أنك صاحب كل خنى is invalid in that construction.
rows.anchor: أنك صاحب كل خنى لم يجز ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أنما is also acceptable in وجد خبره أنما يجالس أهل الخبث because the clause identifies the same matter as the preceding expression.
rows.anchor: وتقول وجدت خبره أنما يجالس أهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kuthayr's verse supplies a further example of إنما introducing an independent clause rather than functioning as a noun.
rows.anchor: وقال كثير # % أراني ولا كفران لله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An active participle for an action currently occurring or continuing functions like the present-tense verb in both meaning and government, taking its object in the accusative.
rows.anchor: فمعناه وعمله مثل هذا يضرب زيدا غدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Poetic examples, including Zuhayr's تنوين on سابقا, show the active participle with tanwin in this ongoing-action use.
rows.anchor: أنى لست مدرك ما مضى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dropping tanwin or the sound plural nun for ease does not change meaning or make the participle definite; its object then takes genitive as it is joined to the noun.
rows.anchor: فيحذفون التنوين والنون ولا يتغير من المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sībawayh cites ناكسو رؤوسهم as an active participle without its nun in annexation, with its object in the genitive.
rows.anchor: لو ترى إذ المجرمون ناكسو رءسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur'anic examples such as ذائقة الموت, مرسلوا الناقة, غير محلي الصيد, and آمين البيت الحرام illustrate the uninflected participle construction.
rows.anchor: فمن ذلك قوله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هديا بالغ الكعبة and عارض ممطرنا show the participle remains indefinite without tanwin, since it can describe an indefinite noun.
rows.anchor: ويزيد هذا عندك بيانا قوله تعالى جده

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil gives هو كائن أخيك as a lightened form whose meaning is هو كائن أخاك.
rows.anchor: وقال الخليل هو كائن أخيك على الاستخفاف والمعنى هو كائن أخاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sībawayh cites non-tanwined participles in poetry by al-Farazdaq, al-Zibriqan, al-Sulayk, al-Nabigha, and al-Marrar as evidence for the construction.
rows.anchor: الشعر غير منون قول الفرزدق

rows.speaker: عيسى
rows.claim: Isa reports that some reciters omit tanwin in Abu al-Aswad's verse to avoid two adjacent sukuns, not to make the participle genitive; Sībawayh calls this poetic necessity.
rows.anchor: هذا البيت لأبى الأسود الدؤلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When a participle and a second noun share its genitive complement, both may be genitive; accusative coordination is also possible by eliding an understood verb or participle.
rows.anchor: وتقول فى هذا باب هذا ضارب زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jarir and Ka'b ibn Juayl provide poetic examples of accusative coordination understood through an omitted verb or participle.
rows.anchor: جاء على المعنى قول جرير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the action is completed rather than ongoing, the active participle has no tanwin and behaves like a noun, so a coordinated complement is genitive.
rows.anchor: أن الفعل قد وقع وانقطع فهو بغير تنوين ألبتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Accusative coordination becomes stronger after a long separation from the participle's complement; Sībawayh cites والشمس والقمر حسبانا as Qur'anic evidence.
rows.anchor: كلما طال الكلام كان أقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With a participle governing two objects, tanwin allows either object order; without tanwin, the complement joined to the participle cannot be separated, as in مخلف وعده رسله.
rows.anchor: هذا معط زيدا درهما ~~لا تبال
